## 1. Data Import

```{r import-data}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)

file_path <- "data/quarterly-median-rents-local-government-area-september-quarter-2025-excel.xlsx"

rental_raw <- read_excel(
  file_path,
  sheet = "All Properties",
  col_names = FALSE
)

dim(rental_raw)

head(rental_raw[, 1:8], 10)

```
## 2. Extract Melbourne LGAs

```{r extract-melbourne}
# Select rows belonging to Melbourne's three metropolitan regions
melbourne_rows <- c(57:70, 72:78, 80:89)

# Extract Melbourne LGA records
melbourne_raw <- rental_raw[melbourne_rows, ]

# Check the dimensions
dim(melbourne_raw)

# Display the LGA names
print(melbourne_raw[[2]])
```
## 3. Examine Quarterly Dates

```{r examine-dates}
# Extract the quarterly date headings
quarter_dates <- unlist(rental_raw[2, 3:ncol(rental_raw)],
                        use.names = FALSE)

# Display the first 12 date headings
print(head(quarter_dates, 12))

# Display the last 12 date headings
print(tail(quarter_dates, 12))
```
## 4. Restructure Rental Data

```{r restructure-data}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Extract quarter labels and measurement types
quarter_labels <- as.character(unlist(
  rental_raw[2, 3:ncol(rental_raw)],
  use.names = FALSE
))

measurement_types <- as.character(unlist(
  rental_raw[3, 3:ncol(rental_raw)],
  use.names = FALSE
))

# Create descriptive column names
new_names <- paste(
  quarter_labels,
  measurement_types,
  sep = "_"
)

# Select Melbourne LGAs
rental_clean <- as.data.frame(melbourne_raw)

# Assign new column names
colnames(rental_clean) <- c(
  "Region",
  "LGA",
  new_names
)

# Convert wide data into long format
rental_long <- rental_clean %>%
  select(-Region) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -LGA,
    names_to = c("Quarter", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "^(.*)_(Count|Median)$"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Count = as.numeric(Count),
    Median = as.numeric(Median),
    Quarter = as.Date(
      paste0("01 ", Quarter),
      format = "%d %b %Y"
    )
  ) %>%
  rename(
    Median_Rent = Median,
    Rental_Count = Count
  ) %>%
  arrange(LGA, Quarter)

# Check the new dataset
dim(rental_long)

head(rental_long, 10)

# Check the date range
range(rental_long$Quarter)
```
## 5. Exploratory Data Analysis

### 5.1 Historical Rental Trends

```{r rental-trends}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Calculate median of LGA median rents for each quarter
melbourne_trend <- rental_long %>%
  group_by(Quarter) %>%
  summarise(
    Median_Rent = median(Median_Rent, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Create historical rental trend chart
ggplot(melbourne_trend, aes(x = Quarter, y = Median_Rent)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "darkblue", size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Historical Rental Trends Across Melbourne LGAs",
    subtitle = "Median of LGA median weekly rents (1999–2025)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Median Weekly Rent (AUD)",
    caption = "Source: Homes Victoria, Quarterly Median Rents by LGA"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```
### 5.2 Geographic Differences in Rental Prices

```{r highest-rent-lgas}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Select the latest quarter
latest_rents <- rental_long %>%
  filter(Quarter == max(Quarter, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Median_Rent))

# Display the 10 most expensive LGAs
print(as.data.frame(head(latest_rents, 10)))

# Create a bar chart
ggplot(
  head(latest_rents, 10),
  aes(x = reorder(LGA, Median_Rent), y = Median_Rent)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Most Expensive Melbourne LGAs",
    subtitle = "Median weekly rent, September 2025",
    x = "Local Government Area",
    y = "Median Weekly Rent (AUD)",
    caption = "Source: Homes Victoria, Quarterly Median Rents by LGA"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```
### 5.3 Annual Rental Growth Across Melbourne LGAs

```{r annual-rental-growth}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

# Select September 2024 and September 2025
annual_growth <- rental_long %>%
  filter(Quarter %in% as.Date(c("2024-09-01", "2025-09-01"))) %>%
  select(LGA, Quarter, Median_Rent) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Quarter,
    values_from = Median_Rent,
    names_prefix = "Rent_"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Growth_Percent =
      ((`Rent_2025-09-01` - `Rent_2024-09-01`) /
         `Rent_2024-09-01`) * 100
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Growth_Percent))

# Display top 10 LGAs
print(as.data.frame(head(annual_growth, 10)))

# Visualise annual rental growth
ggplot(
  head(annual_growth, 10),
  aes(x = reorder(LGA, Growth_Percent),
      y = Growth_Percent)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Melbourne LGAs by Annual Rental Growth",
    subtitle = "September 2024 – September 2025",
    x = "Local Government Area",
    y = "Annual Median Rent Growth (%)",
    caption = "Source: Homes Victoria, Quarterly Median Rents by LGA"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```
### 5.4 Quarterly Rental Growth Analysis

```{r quarterly-rental-growth}
library(dplyr)

quarterly_growth <- rental_long %>%
  arrange(LGA, Quarter) %>%
  group_by(LGA) %>%
  mutate(
    Previous_Rent = lag(Median_Rent),
    Quarterly_Growth = 
      ((Median_Rent - Previous_Rent) / Previous_Rent) * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Display first 10 observations
print(as.data.frame(head(quarterly_growth, 10)))

# Summary of quarterly rental growth
summary(quarterly_growth$Quarterly_Growth)

# Check missing values
sum(is.na(quarterly_growth$Quarterly_Growth))
```
## 6. Defining the Prediction Target

```{r prediction-target}
library(dplyr)

rental_prediction <- quarterly_growth %>%
  arrange(LGA, Quarter) %>%
  group_by(LGA) %>%
  mutate(
    Next_Quarter_Rent = lead(Median_Rent),

    Next_Quarter_Growth =
      ((Next_Quarter_Rent - Median_Rent) /
         Median_Rent) * 100,

    Deterioration = case_when(
      is.na(Next_Quarter_Growth) ~ NA_integer_,
      Next_Quarter_Growth > 0 ~ 1L,
      TRUE ~ 0L
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Check prediction target distribution
table(
  rental_prediction$Deterioration,
  useNA = "ifany"
)

# Display sample records
print(
  as.data.frame(
    head(
      rental_prediction[
        ,
        c(
          "LGA",
          "Quarter",
          "Median_Rent",
          "Next_Quarter_Rent",
          "Next_Quarter_Growth",
          "Deterioration"
        )
      ],
      10
    )
  )
)
```
## 7. Preparing Features for Machine Learning

```{r feature-engineering}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

model_data <- rental_prediction %>%
  arrange(LGA, Quarter) %>%
  group_by(LGA) %>%
  mutate(
    Previous_Quarter_Growth = lag(Quarterly_Growth),
    Year = year(Quarter),
    Quarter_Number = quarter(Quarter)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Deterioration),
    !is.na(Quarterly_Growth),
    !is.na(Previous_Quarter_Growth)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Deterioration = factor(
      Deterioration,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("No_Increase", "Increase")
    )
  )

# Check dimensions
dim(model_data)

# Check target distribution
table(model_data$Deterioration)

# Check missing values
colSums(is.na(model_data[
  ,
  c(
    "Median_Rent",
    "Rental_Count",
    "Quarterly_Growth",
    "Previous_Quarter_Growth",
    "Year",
    "Quarter_Number",
    "Deterioration"
  )
]))

# Display sample records
print(as.data.frame(
  head(
    model_data[
      ,
      c(
        "LGA",
        "Quarter",
        "Median_Rent",
        "Rental_Count",
        "Quarterly_Growth",
        "Previous_Quarter_Growth",
        "Year",
        "Quarter_Number",
        "Deterioration"
      )
    ],
    10
  )
))
```
## 8. Training and Testing Data

```{r train-test-split}
library(dplyr)

# Chronological train/test split
train_data <- model_data %>%
  filter(Quarter < as.Date("2022-12-01"))

test_data <- model_data %>%
  filter(Quarter >= as.Date("2023-01-01"))

# Check dataset sizes
cat("Training observations:", nrow(train_data), "\n")
cat("Testing observations:", nrow(test_data), "\n")

# Check date ranges
cat("Training period:\n")
print(range(train_data$Quarter))

cat("Testing period:\n")
print(range(test_data$Quarter))

# Check class distribution
cat("Training class distribution:\n")
print(table(train_data$Deterioration))

cat("Testing class distribution:\n")
print(table(test_data$Deterioration))

# Confirm no overlap between training and testing periods
cat(
  "Chronological split valid:",
  max(train_data$Quarter) < min(test_data$Quarter),
  "\n"
)
```
## 9. Logistic Regression Model

```{r logistic-regression}
# Ensure the target variable has the correct reference category
train_data$Deterioration <- factor(
  train_data$Deterioration,
  levels = c("No_Increase", "Increase")
)

test_data$Deterioration <- factor(
  test_data$Deterioration,
  levels = c("No_Increase", "Increase")
)

# Train logistic regression model
logistic_model <- glm(
  Deterioration ~ Median_Rent +
    Rental_Count +
    Quarterly_Growth +
    Previous_Quarter_Growth +
    Quarter_Number,
  data = train_data,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

# Display model summary
summary(logistic_model)
```
## 10. Logistic Regression Model Evaluation

```{r model-evaluation}
# Predict probabilities on testing data
test_probabilities <- predict(
  logistic_model,
  newdata = test_data,
  type = "response"
)

# Convert probabilities into classifications
test_predictions <- ifelse(
  test_probabilities >= 0.5,
  "Increase",
  "No_Increase"
)

# Convert predictions into factors
test_predictions <- factor(
  test_predictions,
  levels = c("No_Increase", "Increase")
)

# Confusion matrix
confusion_matrix <- table(
  Actual = test_data$Deterioration,
  Predicted = test_predictions
)

print(confusion_matrix)

# Calculate accuracy
accuracy <- mean(
  test_predictions == test_data$Deterioration
)

# Calculate precision
precision <- sum(
  test_predictions == "Increase" &
    test_data$Deterioration == "Increase"
) / sum(test_predictions == "Increase")

# Calculate recall
recall <- sum(
  test_predictions == "Increase" &
    test_data$Deterioration == "Increase"
) / sum(test_data$Deterioration == "Increase")

# Calculate F1 score
f1_score <- 2 * precision * recall /
  (precision + recall)

# Display evaluation metrics
cat("Accuracy:", round(accuracy, 4), "\n")
cat("Precision:", round(precision, 4), "\n")
cat("Recall:", round(recall, 4), "\n")
cat("F1 Score:", round(f1_score, 4), "\n")

# Majority-class baseline
baseline_accuracy <- max(
  prop.table(table(test_data$Deterioration))
)

cat(
  "Majority-Class Baseline Accuracy:",
  round(baseline_accuracy, 4),
  "\n"
)
```
## 11. Prediction Threshold Analysis

```{r threshold-analysis}

# Function to calculate evaluation metrics
evaluate_threshold <- function(threshold) {

  predictions <- ifelse(
    test_probabilities >= threshold,
    "Increase",
    "No_Increase"
  )

  actual <- as.character(test_data$Deterioration)

  TP <- sum(predictions == "Increase" & actual == "Increase")
  TN <- sum(predictions == "No_Increase" & actual == "No_Increase")
  FP <- sum(predictions == "Increase" & actual == "No_Increase")
  FN <- sum(predictions == "No_Increase" & actual == "Increase")

  accuracy <- (TP + TN) / (TP + TN + FP + FN)

  precision <- if ((TP + FP) == 0) {
    NA_real_
  } else {
    TP / (TP + FP)
  }

  recall <- TP / (TP + FN)

  f1 <- if (is.na(precision) || (precision + recall) == 0) {
    NA_real_
  } else {
    2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
  }

  data.frame(
    Threshold = threshold,
    Accuracy = round(accuracy, 4),
    Precision = round(precision, 4),
    Recall = round(recall, 4),
    F1_Score = round(f1, 4)
  )
}

# Compare different thresholds
threshold_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(c(0.30, 0.40, 0.50, 0.60), evaluate_threshold)
)

print(threshold_results)

```
## 12. Improved Logistic Regression Model

```{r improved-logistic-regression}

# Convert calendar quarter into a categorical variable
train_data$Quarter_Factor <- factor(
  train_data$Quarter_Number
)

test_data$Quarter_Factor <- factor(
  test_data$Quarter_Number,
  levels = levels(train_data$Quarter_Factor)
)

# Train improved logistic regression model
improved_model <- glm(
  Deterioration ~
    Median_Rent +
    Rental_Count +
    Quarterly_Growth +
    Previous_Quarter_Growth +
    Year +
    Quarter_Factor,
  data = train_data,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

# Display model summary
summary(improved_model)

# Generate test probabilities
improved_probabilities <- predict(
  improved_model,
  newdata = test_data,
  type = "response"
)

# Evaluate using the original 0.50 threshold
improved_predictions <- factor(
  ifelse(
    improved_probabilities >= 0.5,
    "Increase",
    "No_Increase"
  ),
  levels = c("No_Increase", "Increase")
)

# Confusion matrix
print(table(
  Actual = test_data$Deterioration,
  Predicted = improved_predictions
))

# Accuracy
improved_accuracy <- mean(
  improved_predictions == test_data$Deterioration
)

cat(
  "Improved Model Accuracy:",
  round(improved_accuracy, 4),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Original Model Accuracy:",
  round(accuracy, 4),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Majority-Class Baseline:",
  round(baseline_accuracy, 4),
  "\n"
)

```

```{r improved-model-comparison}

# Display confusion matrix
cat("Improved Model Confusion Matrix:\n")

print(

  )
)

# Compare model accuracy
cat("\nOriginal Model Accuracy:",

cat("Improved Model Accuracy:",
```

## 14. Historical Momentum Baseline

```{r momentum-baseline}

# Predict an increase if current-quarter growth is positive
momentum_predictions <- factor(
  ifelse(
    test_data$Quarterly_Growth > 0,
    "Increase",
    "No_Increase"
  ),
  levels = c("No_Increase", "Increase")
)

# Confusion matrix
momentum_confusion <- table(
  Actual = test_data$Deterioration,
  Predicted = momentum_predictions
)

print(momentum_confusion)

# Calculate accuracy
momentum_accuracy <- mean(
  momentum_predictions == test_data$Deterioration
)

# Calculate precision and recall
momentum_tp <- sum(
  momentum_predictions == "Increase" &
    test_data$Deterioration == "Increase"
)

momentum_fp <- sum(
  momentum_predictions == "Increase" &
    test_data$Deterioration == "No_Increase"
)

momentum_fn <- sum(
  momentum_predictions == "No_Increase" &
    test_data$Deterioration == "Increase"
)

momentum_precision <- if (
  momentum_tp + momentum_fp == 0
) NA_real_ else momentum_tp / (momentum_tp + momentum_fp)

momentum_recall <- momentum_tp /
  (momentum_tp + momentum_fn)

momentum_f1 <- if (
  is.na(momentum_precision) ||
  momentum_precision + momentum_recall == 0
) NA_real_ else
  2 * momentum_precision * momentum_recall /
  (momentum_precision + momentum_recall)

cat("Momentum Accuracy:",
    round(momentum_accuracy * 100, 2), "%\n")

cat("Momentum Precision:",
    round(momentum_precision * 100, 2), "%\n")

cat("Momentum Recall:",
    round(momentum_recall * 100, 2), "%\n")

cat("Momentum F1 Score:",
    round(momentum_f1 * 100, 2), "%\n")

```
## 15. Model Performance Comparison

```{r model-performance-chart}
library(ggplot2)

model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Original Logistic (0.50)",
    "Improved Logistic (0.50)",
    "Original Logistic (0.30)",
    "Historical Momentum",
    "Majority-Class Baseline"
  ),
  Accuracy = c(
    accuracy,
    improved_accuracy,
    threshold_results$Accuracy[threshold_results$Threshold == 0.30],
    momentum_accuracy,
    baseline_accuracy
  )
)

ggplot(
  model_comparison,
  aes(
    x = reorder(Model, Accuracy),
    y = Accuracy
  )
) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(round(Accuracy * 100, 1), "%")),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 3.8
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    limits = c(0, 0.75)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of Rental Increase Prediction Approaches",
    subtitle = "Melbourne LGAs, test period: 2023–2025",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Prediction Accuracy",
    caption = "Source: Homes Victoria rental data; author's analysis."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```
## 16. Findings and Discussion

### 16.1 Historical Rental Trends

The analysis examined 3,286 quarterly observations covering 31 Melbourne
Local Government Areas (LGAs) between June 1999 and September 2025.

The median of LGA-level median weekly rents increased substantially over
the study period, with particularly strong growth visible after 2022.

In September 2025, Bayside recorded the highest median weekly rent
($743), followed by Manningham ($680) and Melbourne ($670).

### 16.2 Recent Rental Growth

Between September 2024 and September 2025, Bayside experienced the
largest percentage increase in median weekly rent (10.90%), followed
by Moonee Valley (10.00%) and Manningham (8.80%).

These results demonstrate that areas with the highest rents are not
necessarily the same areas experiencing the fastest rental growth.

### 16.3 Predictive Modelling

A logistic regression model was developed to predict whether an LGA's
median weekly rent would increase in the following quarter.

The model used historical rental indicators, including median rent,
rental count, quarterly rental growth, previous-quarter growth,
and calendar-quarter information.

A chronological training/testing split was applied to evaluate predictive performance. The training dataset contained 2,852 observations from December 1999 to September 2022, while the testing dataset contained 310 observations from March 2023 to June 2025. The December 2022 observations were excluded from training because their prediction targets required March 2023 outcomes. This separation ensured that the training labels did not depend on rental observations from the testing period.

The original logistic regression model achieved 45.16% test accuracy.
A revised model incorporating categorical calendar-quarter effects
and year achieved 48.71%.

Lowering the original model's classification threshold to 0.30
increased accuracy to 61.61% and recall to 87.88%.
However, this threshold was examined using the test set, so the
result should be interpreted as exploratory.

The historical momentum baseline achieved 58.71% accuracy, while
the majority-class baseline achieved 63.87%.

None of the evaluated approaches exceeded the majority-class
baseline in test accuracy.

### 16.4 Limitations

The analysis has several limitations:

1. The dataset contains rental-market indicators but does not include
   household income. Therefore, the models predict rental-price
   increases rather than actual rental stress or affordability.

2. The models use a limited set of historical rental indicators.
   Additional socioeconomic, demographic, and housing-supply
   variables may improve future modelling.

3. Rental-market conditions may change over time, reducing the
   reliability of models trained on older observations.

4. The models were evaluated using a single chronological test
   period. Future work should use rolling-origin validation and
   a separate, untouched final test period.

5. The reported median rent represents each LGA's rental market
   and does not capture affordability differences between
   individual households.

### 16.5 Conclusion

This demonstration establishes a reproducible workflow for collecting,
cleaning, exploring, and modelling Melbourne rental-market data.

The exploratory analysis identified substantial long-term rental
growth and differences between LGAs.

Although the predictive models did not outperform the majority-class
baseline, the results highlight the importance of careful model
evaluation and the need for richer data.

Future development should integrate household-income and
socioeconomic indicators to support a more direct assessment
of rental affordability and potential rental stress.
